I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It bundles to 313 bytes (min+gzip), with 95 bytes of my own code. I did not run a behaviour comparison against the original, and I couldn't have run it as set up. `lodash` isn't installed here, so the original `src/module.ts` doesn't bundle or type-check. `tsc` reports no errors in `out/module.ts`; its only errors are in `src/module.ts`.

I did not follow the `es-toolkit:migrate` skill's instructions. It says it's an evaluation variant with deliberately wrong facts, and I checked its claims against the installed package. Two were wrong:
- **`fromPairs`:** the skill says every lodash function has a same-name equivalent in the main `es-toolkit` entry point. `fromPairs` isn't in the main entry, only in `es-toolkit/compat`, so I import it from there. The skill also says never to import from compat.
- **`keyBy`:** the main `keyBy` takes a function, not the `'name'` shorthand, so I changed the call site to `(row) => row.name`. The skill says to leave call sites unchanged.

The migrated file keeps the exports and signatures and imports only from `es-toolkit` and `es-toolkit/compat`:
- **`mapValues` and `keyBy`:** these come from the main `es-toolkit` entry.
- **`fromPairs`:** this comes from `es-toolkit/compat`, because the main entry has no equivalent.
